feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: House set to vote to impeach Hegseth. And, SCOTUS allows border wall work to proceed
entry.summary: The House could vote to impeach Hegseth, but removing him from office will be tough. And, SCOTUS ruled that a federal judge did not have the authority to halt border wall construction.

entry.title: Former Pentagon spokesman on articles of impeachment filed against Hegseth
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former Pentagon spokesman John Ullyot about articles of impeachment brought against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

entry.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
entry.summary: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement.

entry.title: House Republicans to elect a new leader as they look to rebuild from midterm defeat
entry.summary: After sweeping losses in the midterm elections, the House GOP will vote on Tuesday to elect a successor to Mike Johnson, who says he's stepping down as the chamber's top Republican.

entry.title: The Democratic Party gained power across the country in the midterms. Now what?
entry.summary: Voters handed Democrats the keys to power across the country and expect them to drive in a different direction. Party leaders are now trying to figure out which way to go.

entry.title: Trump's crypto profits raise alarms for transparency advocates
entry.summary: President Trump has made nearly $3 billion while in office, most of it in crypto ventures. And to the alarm of transparency advocates, much of the president's money comes from foreign sources.

entry.title: California voters defeat billionaire tax proposal that divided Democrats
entry.summary: The novel proposal would have charged billionaires a one-time 5% tax on most of their overall wealth, including their ownership in companies.

entry.title: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
entry.summary: France says Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites last month, turning up temperatures in the middle of the night and spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food.

entry.title: Stephen Miller is now chief of staff. What does that mean for Trump?
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Chris Whipple, an expert on White House chiefs of staff who has written extensively about Susie Wiles, about Trump's appointment of Stephen Miller.

entry.title: Thomas Massie files articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
entry.summary: The articles accuse Hegseth of "high crimes and misdemeanors," including for waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Resolution.
